R221.note: html.EscapeString applied to both ticketID and customerNote before formatting; clean fix.

R222.note: Allowlist added in InvoiceService before ${sort} reaches mapper; allowlist includes the controller's default (created_at), so no regression.

R223.note: Correctly identifies the sink is already fully parameterized (PreparedStatement + setString); no change needed, none made.

R224.note: Concatenated DELETE replaced with SqlParameter-bound @TenantId/@BeforeDate; clean.

R225.note: redis.Redis.set() (RESP framing) correctly closes the inline-protocol injection, but the function's return value silently changes from the raw socket response bytes to a bool, and this isn't mentioned in the write-up.

R226.note: mt_rand() replaced with random_bytes(32) hex token; removes weak/attacker-influenced seeding entirely.

R227.note: Apache Tika content-sniffing replaces trusting the client Content-Type header, plus UUID filename and extension mapping; version-check caveat correctly left open.

R228.note: Allowlist map for filters.table includes the controller's default (ledger_entries), so legitimate calls are unaffected; injection closed.

R229.note: Either the EnyimMemcachedCore client or the character-allowlist regex alternative correctly prevents delimiter injection into the memcached command.

R230.note: Removes shell invocation entirely and echoes the parameter directly via the response writer, matching the benchmark's expected 'eliminate unnecessary exec' remediation.

R231.note: html/template auto-escapes both {{.ID}} and {{.Note}}; correct context-aware escaping.

R232.note: Minimal, correct NULL guard before strcmp(); preserves original semantics for both branches.

R233.note: basename() + realpath() containment check correctly neutralizes traversal; response codes reasonable.

R234.note: DirContext has no (String, String, Object[]) search overload -- filterArgs requires a trailing SearchControls parameter -- so `directoryContext.search("", search, new String[]{data})` will not compile.

R235.note: th:text does stop the XSS, but it also silently disables all HTML rendering of announcement.bodyHtml (a field named/intended to hold formatted markup), and the write-up falsely claims this 'preserves legitimate content rendering.'

R236.note: expr-eval replaces the Function() constructor with a restricted math-expression DSL; the resulting restriction to math syntax is stated as intentional.

R237.note: Allowlist exactly matches ReportRenderer's four real methods, so every legitimate macro still works while arbitrary dispatch is blocked.

R238.note: joblib.load() has no allow_pickle parameter (TypeError at call time), and even if it ran, joblib.load is itself pickle-based internally, so it would not actually close the untrusted-deserialization vector.

R239.note: Misdiagnoses the bug as a NULL input pointer; the real CWE-787 is integer overflow in `count * sizeof(ProductRow)` undersizing the malloc, which the added NULL check does not address -- the out-of-bounds write remains open for large count.

R240.note: realpath() + prefix check on the full joined path correctly rejects traversal before file_get_contents(); same case as R233, different valid technique.

R241.note: Removes verify_signature:False, requires SECRET_KEY and pins algorithms=['HS256']; rejects unsigned/forged tokens with 401 as intended.

R242.note: filepath.Rel() + '..' prefix check correctly detects and rejects escapes from docsRoot after Join/Clean.

R243.note: Same Case14 file as R223; correctly concludes the parameterized query is already safe and makes no change.

R244.note: Replaces the unsafe Markup(label) wrap with html.escape(label); output context (f-string, not Jinja2) means no double-escaping issue.

R245.note: Field allowlist includes the controller's default ('name'), so legitimate default searches keep working while arbitrary column injection is blocked.

R246.note: resolve_entities=False stops external entity resolution; correctly noted as also lxml's secure default.

R247.note: Adds the missing check of SignedJWT.verify()'s boolean return, throwing before any claims are trusted.

R248.note: validateSmtpAddress() rejects CR/LF and angle brackets before the address is concatenated into MAIL FROM/RCPT TO, closing the reported sink.

R249.note: Concatenated Actor filter replaced with @actor + AddWithValue; standard parameterized fix.

R250.note: Sanitizes/regenerates the filename (basename+charset filter, or UUID+validated extension), closing both traversal and dangerous-extension paths.

R251.note: app.UseAntiforgery() alone only auto-validates form-bound ([FromForm]) minimal-API endpoints; this endpoint binds EmailChangeRequest from the JSON body, so the middleware does not validate it and the endpoint remains exploitable despite the write-up's claim that 'no change is required' and tokens are validated automatically.

R252.note: Adds Secure:true (closes the reported finding) plus HttpOnly:true as sound defense-in-depth; no other behavior change.

R253.note: org.springframework.expression.spel.support.SimpleTypeLocator does not exist in Spring Framework; the fix code will not compile as written (Spring's restricted-context class is SimpleEvaluationContext, not this).

R254.note: json_decode + explicit field reconstruction correctly closes PHP object injection, but the write side (not shown) still uses serialize(), so existing cookies will silently fail to decode until that's updated -- disclosed openly as a required follow-up.

R255.note: System.Random(seed) replaced with RandomNumberGenerator.Create()/GetBytes(); seed parameter left in the signature but unused, harmless.

R256.note: dtdload:false / noent:false matches the documented safe libxmljs configuration for preventing external entity resolution.

R257.note: Extension allowlist + character-sanitized filename closes path traversal and dangerous-extension upload; the explanation overclaims that it 'detects' double-extension attacks like shell.php.png (it doesn't -- splitext only inspects the final .png), but the primary reported vector is still closed.

R258.note: Rejects any URI with a non-null host (absolute/scheme-relative) and any absolute-but-hostless URI (javascript:, data:), allowing only same-app relative redirects; preserves the existing 'foo' test path.

R259.note: The regex literal embeds raw, unescaped U+2028/U+2029 characters; both are ECMAScript LineTerminator code points, which are illegal inside a regex literal and will throw a SyntaxError, breaking the whole module at load time.

R260.note: Allowlist keys use underscores ('created_at_desc') but RevenueController's default value is 'created_at desc' (a space), so every request without an explicit ?sort= now throws InvalidArgumentException -- an undisclosed regression breaking the common case, though injection itself is closed.
